lines.text: Sharma uncle — the shop owner — is shrewd. Aarav is his best worker. He does not want to lose him. Over weeks, he plants seeds.
You know, these engineers think they're above us. But who do they come to when their laptops break? Us.
College boys can't hold a screwdriver. Stay here. Five years, I'll make you a partner.
The partnership offer is real. But Sharma uncle's motive is not Aarav's welfare — it is keeping a skilled worker.
Elster calls this manipulation: an external agent deliberately shaping someone's preferences for the manipulator's advantage.
Unlike sour grapes, which happens inside a person's own mind, manipulation is social and intentional. Someone else is pulling the thread.
